plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). In second-price/Vickrey auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' strategies. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. With my value at $48, I should bid exactly $48 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only that competing bid, maximizing expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Since this is a one-shot game with independent private values, there's no reason to shade my bid. I will bid exactly my value of $38 to ensure optimal expected earnings.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a single-round game with independent draws, there's no need to shade my bid strategically based on history. I will bid exactly my value of $12 to maximize expected profit.
